main_text.l: HActenus fuit primarium sublunare inanimatum corpus, in Elementis explicatum : sequitur Secundarium corpus sublunare inanimatum, in mixtis inanimatis explicandum.
Mixtum seu concretum corpus est per mixtionem.
Mixtio est miscibilium alteratorum unio, cuius doctrina dicitur, μιξολογία.
Miscibilia dicuntur, quorum natura est habilis & idonea ad agendum & patiendum invicem, quae terminum alienum fusilem admittunt, atq; minutim dividi possunt.
Alterata mixtilia dicuntur, quae mutua per contrarias facultates facta actio-ne & passione, fortem alterationem cum substantiae permutatione conjun-ctam subeunt.
Unio est hoc loco quaedam συνέχεια & concordia, qua mixtilia nunc unum sunt facta specie, ac in unam transmigrave-runt naturam.
Mixtionis, tum Requisita, tum Con-sequens, & Oppositum videbimus.

page.notes: The initial H is a large drop capital and is joined to "Actenus" as "HActenus". The "c" before "Mixtio" and "Miscibilia" in the margin of the text, and the small mark before "1.", are unclear and were not transcribed as text. The catchword "ccm," at lower right is uncertain. The faint "Hac6H" at lower left is show-through and was left out. Greek accents in μιξολογία and συνέχεια are as far as they can be read at this resolution.
